question.text: During which stage of the industry life cycle is competition typically the highest and profit margins are at normal levels?

explanation.text: The Logic: The maturity stage is generally the longest phase of the industry life cycle. Growth normally matches the overall economy's growth rate, and competition is high — which reduces profit margins to normal levels. The Trap: Growth stage typically still has above-normal margins and less mature competition. Introduction and decline have their own distinct profitability profiles and are not the highest-competition phase. Note: In maturity, firms tend to differentiate on cost structure and efficiency rather than rapid top-line growth.
